To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a neural network model of event prediction is a promising approach for narrative generation, and 2) the model can be effectively trained on a corpus of text using vector-space representations of events.

(a) the event representation models we propose are effective at predicting the next event in a sequence; (b) the models can be learned effectively from data using a neural network; (c) the models outperform a number of strong baselines; (d) the models are effective at learning the representations of event sequences; and (e) the models can generalize to unseen events and event sequences.
We present a neural-network model for learning a vector-space representation of events, which can be used as a component in a narrative generation system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of automatically learning representations of event sequences from unstructured text, with the goal of providing a model for use in a narrative generation system.
the problem of learning representations of event sequences in a narrative text from the text itself.
the problem of event prediction in a text.

the compositional model is able to learn the coherence of events in a chain from scratch, without relying on any external knowledge sources, and is competitive with models that use external resources.
